name: gradle-bootstrap
title: Gradle project bootstrap
description: Create the Gradle (Kotlin DSL) project with Java 25 toolchain, Spring Boot 4.x, WebFlux, AWS SDK v2 (dynamodb-enhanced async, sqs), JUnit 5, Mockito, reactor-test, Testcontainers and JaCoCo. Create the com.ticketflow package skeleton (domain, usecase, infrastructure) and a health endpoint.
acceptance: ./gradlew build succeeds on Java 25
JaCoCo coverage verification task fails below 90% line coverage
Package skeleton com.ticketflow.{domain,usecase,infrastructure} exists
GET /actuator/health returns 200 (covered by a WebTestClient test)

name: docker-compose-infra
title: Dockerfile and docker-compose with DynamoDB Local and LocalStack SQS
description: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the app (non-root user) and docker-compose.yml that starts the app, DynamoDB Local and LocalStack (SQS). Include an init script that creates the queues (orders queue + DLQ). Provide .env.example.
acceptance: docker compose up --build starts app, DynamoDB Local and LocalStack
Orders queue and its DLQ exist after startup
Container runs as non-root
.env.example documented and .env ignored by git

name: ci-and-ghcr
title: GitHub Actions CI and ghcr.io image publishing
description: Workflow ci.yml running ./init.sh on every PR and push to main (Java 25, Docker available for Testcontainers). Workflow release.yml that builds and pushes ghcr.io/alhucave/ticketflow on tags v*.
acceptance: CI runs ./init.sh on pull_request and push to main
Coverage report uploaded as workflow artifact
release.yml publishes image to ghcr.io on v* tags using GITHUB_TOKEN
Workflows pin action versions and use minimal permissions

name: domain-ticket-state-machine
title: Ticket status enum and transition rules
description: Implement TicketStatus (AVAILABLE, RESERVED, PENDING_CONFIRMATION, SOLD, COMPLIMENTARY) with a pure transition function using pattern matching and a domain exception for invalid transitions. Include flags: isFinal, isSale (only SOLD).
acceptance: Only transitions in docs/architecture.md are allowed; any other throws InvalidStateTransitionException
SOLD and COMPLIMENTARY are final: no outgoing transitions
RESERVED and PENDING_CONFIRMATION are not sales; COMPLIMENTARY is not countable as a sale
Exhaustive test over the full 5x5 transition matrix

name: domain-models-and-ports
title: Domain records, errors and repository ports
description: Create records Event, Inventory (counters + version), Order, OrderAuditEntry, value objects (EventId, OrderId, Quantity, IdempotencyKey) and ports EventRepository, InventoryRepository, OrderRepository, OrderQueuePublisher returning Mono/Flux. Define domain exceptions (EventNotFound, InsufficientInventory, OrderNotFound, ReservationExpired, ConcurrentModification).
acceptance: Records validate invariants in compact constructors (positive quantity, non-blank name, capacity > 0)
Inventory enforces available+reserved+pendingConfirmation+sold+complimentary = capacity
Domain package has no Spring or AWS imports (verified by an ArchUnit or equivalent test)

name: dynamodb-config-tables
title: DynamoDB async client configuration and table provisioning
description: Configure DynamoDbEnhancedAsyncClient with endpoint override for local, region and credentials via properties/env. Provision tables events, inventory, orders (with GSIs) and order_audit on startup when enabled by property.
acceptance: Client endpoint, region and credentials come from configuration, never hardcoded
Tables and GSIs are created idempotently at startup (integration test with Testcontainers)
Provisioning can be disabled by property

name: event-repository
title: DynamoDB EventRepository adapter
description: Implement EventRepository: save event together with its initial inventory (all capacity as available) and find by id / list.
acceptance: Creating an event creates its inventory with available = capacity
findById returns empty Mono for unknown ids
Integration test against DynamoDB Local/LocalStack

name: inventory-repository
title: Inventory repository with conditional writes
description: Implement InventoryRepository operations reserve(eventId, qty), confirmSale, release, issueComplimentary, each as a single UpdateItem with ConditionExpression and version increment. Map ConditionalCheckFailed to InsufficientInventory or ConcurrentModification. Retry with backoff only on transient errors.
acceptance: reserve fails with InsufficientInventory when available < qty
Each mutation is one atomic conditional write incrementing version
Counter invariant holds after any sequence of operations (property-style test)
Transient throttling is retried; business errors are not

name: order-repository
title: Order repository with audit trail and idempotency lookup
description: Implement OrderRepository: create, findById, findByIdempotencyKey (GSI), transition status with a conditional write on the expected current status, append audit entries, and query expired reservations (GSI status + expiresAt).
acceptance: Status transition uses a condition on the expected current status
Every transition appends an audit entry with from, to, timestamp and actor
findByIdempotencyKey returns the existing order
findExpired returns only RESERVED/PENDING_CONFIRMATION orders with expiresAt < now

name: usecase-events
title: Create and query events use cases
description: CreateEventUseCase, GetEventUseCase, ListEventsUseCase with validation (name, date in the future, venue, capacity > 0).
acceptance: Rejects invalid input with a domain validation error
Returns event with current inventory snapshot
Unit tests with mocked ports using StepVerifier

name: usecase-availability
title: Real-time availability use case
description: GetAvailabilityUseCase returning a snapshot (available, reserved, pendingConfirmation, sold, complimentary) and a Flux stream variant that emits on changes (polling interval configurable).
acceptance: Availability reflects reserved and pending tickets as not available
Stream variant emits updates and completes/cancels cleanly
Unknown event yields EventNotFound

name: usecase-purchase-request
title: Purchase request use case (reserve + enqueue)
description: RequestPurchaseUseCase: validate, honor Idempotency-Key (return existing order), atomically reserve inventory with 10-minute expiry, persist order as RESERVED, publish to the order queue and return orderId immediately. If publishing fails after reserving, release the reservation and mark the order failed.
acceptance: Returns orderId without waiting for processing
Same Idempotency-Key never creates a second order or reserves twice
Reservation expiry is exactly now + 10 minutes (configurable, tested with a fixed Clock)
Publish failure compensates by releasing inventory

name: usecase-order-status
title: Order status query use case
description: GetOrderStatusUseCase returning current status (any of the five states), quantity, event and expiry; OrderNotFound otherwise.
acceptance: Returns the current status for existing orders
Unknown order id yields OrderNotFound
Unit tests cover each status value

name: usecase-process-order
title: Process order use case (consumer logic)
description: ProcessOrderUseCase: idempotent handling of an order message: RESERVED -> PENDING_CONFIRMATION -> SOLD, validating the reservation is still valid (not expired) and real inventory. Reprocessing a SOLD order is a no-op. Expired reservations end released.
acceptance: Processing the same message twice yields the same final state and counters
Expired reservation is not sold and its inventory is released
Transitions are audited
Concurrent processing of the same order results in a single sale

name: sqs-publisher
title: SQS order queue publisher adapter
description: Implement OrderQueuePublisher with the AWS SDK v2 async SQS client. Message body is a versioned JSON record with orderId; include message attributes for tracing. Retry with backoff on transient errors.
acceptance: Publishing returns after SQS acknowledges the message
Integration test with LocalStack verifies the message arrives
Endpoint and queue URL come from configuration

name: sqs-consumer
title: SQS consumer with at-least-once semantics and DLQ
description: Reactive long-polling consumer that calls ProcessOrderUseCase and deletes the message only after success. Configure visibility timeout, maxReceiveCount and DLQ redrive. Bounded concurrency; graceful shutdown.
acceptance: Message is deleted only after successful processing
Failed processing makes the message reappear and, after maxReceiveCount, land in the DLQ (integration test)
Concurrency is bounded by configuration
Poison messages (invalid JSON) do not stop the consumer

name: reservation-expiration-job
title: Scheduled release of expired reservations
description: Reactive scheduler that periodically finds expired reservations and, per order, atomically transitions it to expired and returns inventory to available. Safe under multiple app instances (conditional transition ensures one winner).
acceptance: Expired reservations return their quantity to available exactly once
Non-expired reservations are untouched
Two concurrent runs never release the same order twice
Interval is configurable and tested with a virtual clock

name: web-events-api
title: Events REST endpoints
description: POST /events, GET /events/{id}, GET /events with request/response DTOs as records and bean validation.
acceptance: POST /events returns 201 with Location header
Invalid body returns 400 with a structured error
Unknown id returns 404
WebTestClient tests for each endpoint

name: web-orders-availability-api
title: Orders and availability REST endpoints
description: POST /orders (Idempotency-Key header, returns 202 + orderId), GET /orders/{id}, GET /events/{id}/availability and GET /events/{id}/availability/stream (text/event-stream).
acceptance: POST /orders returns 202 immediately with orderId
Missing or malformed Idempotency-Key returns 400
Availability stream produces server-sent events
WebTestClient tests for each endpoint

name: web-error-handling
title: Global reactive error handling
description: Central handler mapping domain exceptions to RFC 7807 problem details: 404, 409 (insufficient inventory, concurrent modification), 410 (expired reservation), 400, 429 and 500 without leaking internals.
acceptance: Each domain exception maps to the documented status
500 responses never expose stack traces or internal messages
A correlation id is included in error responses and logs

name: complimentary-issuance
title: Issue complimentary tickets
description: Use case and endpoint POST /events/{id}/complimentary that moves tickets AVAILABLE -> COMPLIMENTARY. Final state, excluded from sales totals.
acceptance: Cannot exceed available inventory
Complimentary tickets are not counted as sold in any report or counter
Transition is audited

name: concurrency-tests
title: End-to-end concurrency and consistency tests
description: Integration tests that fire many parallel purchase requests over limited capacity and assert no oversell, correct counters, no duplicate orders for the same Idempotency-Key and correct release after expiry.
acceptance: N parallel requests over capacity C never produce sold + reserved > C
Counter invariant holds at the end of every scenario
Duplicate message delivery does not double-sell
Tests are deterministic (no flaky sleeps)

name: security-hardening
title: Security hardening
description: Secrets only via env vars, request size limits, per-client rate limiting on POST /orders, max quantity per order, input validation, idempotency protection against malicious retries, dependency vulnerability scan in CI, and non-root, minimal runtime image.
acceptance: Rate limit returns 429 when exceeded (tested)
Max quantity per order enforced
No secrets in repository (secret scanning step in CI)
docs/security.md documents threats and mitigations (retries, idempotency, resource abuse)

name: observability
title: Metrics, structured logging and tracing hooks
description: Actuator + Micrometer metrics (orders created/sold/expired, queue lag, conditional-write conflicts), structured JSON logs with correlation id, readiness/liveness probes.
acceptance: Custom business metrics exposed and unit-tested
Logs are structured and include the correlation id
Health groups for liveness and readiness

name: docs-and-requests
title: README, diagrams and request collection
description: Complete README (solution, install, Docker commands, architectural decisions, endpoint examples), Mermaid architecture and sequence diagrams explaining component interactions, and a Postman/Insomnia or curl collection demonstrating the main flows.
acceptance: README covers all items required by the specification
Architecture and sequence diagrams render on GitHub
Request collection exercises create event, purchase, order status and availability
Following the README from a clean clone works

name: aws-cloud-native-docs
title: AWS cloud-native documentation (deferred)
description: Document the target AWS deployment (ECS Fargate, DynamoDB, SQS+DLQ, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, IaC), cloud security best practices, cost estimate, observability and governance. Documentation only, no real deployment.
acceptance: docs/aws.md with architecture diagram
Security, cost, observability and governance sections
Explicitly states that nothing is deployed to AWS
